Candidate Interpretation · Generated From Current Counts

What This Means For SAP Candidates

At this snapshot, the strongest candidate read is that Technical / Development leads the detailed open-feed evidence with 668 of 1,701 postings (39.3%), Technical / Development leads direct employer pages with 1,664 of 4,046 jobs (41.1%), and S/4HANA is the clearest open-feed module anchor. This section is generated from the latest role, module, skill, degree, salary, LinkedIn, and company-career summaries at build time, so the interpretation changes with the daily delta instead of staying as fixed career advice.

Candidate Interpretation

Prioritize the role family that appears across evidence layers.

Both detailed evidence layers point to Technical / Development as the leading role family: 668 of 1,701 open-feed postings (39.3%) and 1,664 of 4,046 direct employer jobs (41.1%). In the LinkedIn collected pool, the largest classified role after broad "Other SAP-Related" is Technical / Development with 56,009 links (14.6%).

Pick a module lane instead of staying generic.

Open-feed module mentions are led by S/4HANA 564 (33.2%), BTP / Integration 290 (17.0%), ABAP / Development 238 (14.0%), HANA / Data 226 (13.3%). Direct employer postings currently skew toward HCM / SuccessFactors 939 (23.2%), S/4HANA 708 (17.5%), BTP / Integration 434 (10.7%), HANA / Data 360 (8.9%). In LinkedIn records where an identifiable SAP area is present, the leading signals are FI / CO / FICO 10,255 (2.7%), S/4HANA 9,776 (2.5%), ABAP / Development 6,408 (1.7%), BTP / Integration 5,330 (1.4%). The clearest cross-source overlap is S/4HANA, BTP / Integration. That makes those areas stronger candidate bets than a source-specific spike alone.

Build a portfolio around current technical terms.

The strongest open-feed technical mentions are S/4HANA 564 (33.2%), Agile / Scrum 235 (13.8%), SAP BTP 213 (12.5%), ABAP 206 (12.1%). Direct employer postings emphasize SuccessFactors 897 (22.2%), S/4HANA 708 (17.5%), Agile / Scrum 356 (8.8%), SAP BTP 348 (8.6%), while the LinkedIn collected pool shows S/4HANA 9,776 (2.5%), FICO 7,377 (1.9%), ABAP 5,906 (1.5%), SAP HANA 3,745 (1.0%). A practical candidate portfolio should show one core module plus integration, data, migration, or implementation evidence.

Soft skills are a market signal, not decoration.

Open-feed descriptions mention Consulting mindset 471 (27.7%), Leadership 270 (15.9%), Change management 206 (12.1%), Analytical thinking 66 (3.9%). Direct employer pages add Consulting mindset 558 (13.8%), Change management 295 (7.3%), Leadership 165 (4.1%), Project management 81 (2.0%), and the LinkedIn pool surfaces Consulting mindset 58,796 (15.3%), Leadership 24,314 (6.3%), Project management 13,223 (3.4%), Change management 11,065 (2.9%). For SAP roles, stakeholder work, rollout/change experience, documentation, training, and cross-functional communication should be visible in CVs and interviews.

Degrees point to useful entry routes, but skills drive the screen.

Open-feed education-field signals are Computer Science / Informatics 300 (17.6%), Engineering 236 (13.9%), Finance / Accounting 220 (12.9%), Logistics / Supply Chain 139 (8.2%). Direct employer pages show Computer Science / Informatics 1,250 (30.9%), Engineering 806 (19.9%), Finance / Accounting 192 (4.7%), Logistics / Supply Chain 135 (3.3%), and LinkedIn collected records show Engineering 41,454 (10.8%), Computer Science / Informatics 25,977 (6.8%), Finance / Accounting 21,327 (5.6%), Logistics / Supply Chain 21,320 (5.6%). The pattern favors computer science/informatics, engineering, finance/accounting, and logistics/supply-chain routes, depending on the SAP module path.

Salary research needs a separate phase.

Salary visibility is partial: 32.4% of the open-feed sample includes pay information (551 of 1,701 postings). Salary cuts by module and country are useful, but still need caveats.

Early-Career Direction

The current data suggests choosing one of several concrete entry lanes rather than trying to be "an SAP person" in general.

  • Technical path: start with S/4HANA, ABAP, BTP, HANA/data, or Fiori/UI5 if your background is computer science, informatics, or engineering.
  • Functional path: use finance/accounting, logistics/supply-chain, HR, procurement, sales, or manufacturing knowledge to enter FI/CO, MM, SD, EWM, PP/QM, or SuccessFactors roles.
  • Consulting path: combine a module with stakeholder workshops, documentation, testing, migration, training, and change-management examples.
  • Signal gap: The LinkedIn pool is link-rich but still description-light: 20,971 rows have fetched description detail (5.5% of the collected LinkedIn pool). Skill and soft-skill signals from LinkedIn should be read as early directional evidence.

LinkedIn Shows The Market Scale; The Collected Pool Shows The Links

The LinkedIn layer separates two different metrics. 371,000+ is LinkedIn's rounded live search-count estimate for SAP + Worldwide; it is not a downloadable list of unique jobs. 383,636 is the deduplicated set of LinkedIn posting links we actually collected, can cite, and can download. The gap is expected because LinkedIn counts are rounded, search results overlap across filters, and not every result is retrievable as a stable guest link.

Why LinkedIn Has Overlap

LinkedIn search results are not a clean one-row-per-job database. The same posting can appear under several searches before deduplication, and some near-duplicate postings are genuinely separate location or employer variants.

  • The same posting can appear across multiple keywords such as SAP, SAP SD, S/4HANA, FICO, ABAP, and BTP.
  • The same posting can appear across location searches when a role is advertised for multiple cities, countries, or regions.
  • The same posting can appear across filters such as all jobs, remote, hybrid, past week, and past month.
  • Some companies publish one role as many location-specific postings; some staffing and aggregator listings describe the same underlying opening more than once.
  • For analysis, the report deduplicates mainly by LinkedIn job id and treats the remaining 383,636 records as the evidence pool, while 371,000+ remains only the market-size signal.

What This Baseline Says

SAP demand is broad, not niche.

LinkedIn's 371,000+ rounded worldwide count is the market-size signal. The 383,636 LinkedIn guest links, 4,046 direct company career postings, and 1,701 open-feed postings are the current evidence layers used for detailed analysis.

Technical / Development leads the open dataset.

Technical / Development is the largest open-feed role family with 668 of 1,701 postings (39.3%). Direct employer postings are currently led by Technical / Development with 1,664 of 4,046 jobs (41.1%).

Salary remains the biggest blind spot.

Only 32.4% of deduplicated open postings include salary information. The next phase should focus on salary ranges by module, country, seniority, and work model.

Contribute to the Research

If you work in SAP, hire SAP talent, or recently interviewed for SAP roles, message me on LinkedIn. I am collecting anonymous input on salary ranges, interview processes, working conditions, role risk, stress level, remote/hybrid reality, and what people genuinely enjoy in their SAP work.

  • No names or company-identifying details will be published without explicit permission.
  • Anonymous insights will be aggregated into future versions of this report.
  • The goal is to make SAP career decisions more transparent for candidates, consultants, and hiring teams.

Methodology

  • Open job data was collected from public job-board feeds and normalized into one common structure: title, company, location, salary fields, source link, SAP focus, role family, seniority, module, and skills.
  • Deduplication removes repeated or near-identical postings by comparing normalized title, company, location, and source URL signals, so the same job is less likely to be counted multiple times across feeds.
  • SAP matching used strong keyword signals such as SAP, S/4HANA, ABAP, SuccessFactors, Ariba, Fiori, UI5, BTP, HANA, BW/4HANA, and related terms.
  • Salary was not estimated. A posting was marked as salary-disclosed only when the source provided salary fields or the description explicitly mentioned compensation.
  • LinkedIn has two separate layers: rounded LinkedIn Jobs search-result counts, and a collected public guest job-link pool gathered through partitioned searches.
  • LinkedIn result overlap is expected. The same posting may appear across multiple keyword, location, work-model, and recency searches; deduplication mainly uses LinkedIn job id to avoid counting those repeated appearances as separate evidence records.
  • Company career data is collected from public career pages and ATS endpoints such as jobs2web / SuccessFactors, SmartRecruiters, Greenhouse, and Workday CXS. These runs are parallel to the LinkedIn crawler and stored as a separate source-linked layer.
  • The LinkedIn guest scraper does not use logged-in cookies, proxy rotation, CAPTCHA bypass, or private profile/session data. The 371,000+ figure is treated as market size; the collected guest pool is the source-linked subset available for analysis and download.

How This Will Stay Alive

  • This first release is a baseline snapshot. Every future run writes a dated snapshot under data/snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD instead of replacing history.
  • A daily delta LaunchAgent runs at 06:15 local time. It uses a lightweight LinkedIn past_24h pass and a merge-mode company career / ATS pass instead of re-running the full market crawl every day.
  • Latest daily delta run: 2026-09-25T07:35:25. LinkedIn status: completed, net new links: 5,949. Company career status: completed, net new jobs: 27.
  • Trend charts will compare snapshots across time: module demand, country mix, seniority, remote/hybrid/on-site, salary transparency, LinkedIn signal shifts, and collected LinkedIn guest-pool growth.
  • The public page can be mirrored to GitHub Pages or any static host, with the source and data snapshots versioned in Git for transparency.
  • Community inputs will be anonymized and added as a separate qualitative layer, so market data and human experience remain distinguishable.
